data.title: Press conference - Bell Bay, Tasmania
data.author: PMC
data.summary: JESS TEESDALE, FEDERAL MEMBER FOR BASS: Thank you so much everyone for being here today. I look around and see so many people who have worked tirelessly for months and months for this day to get here. Do you know what? Uncertainty is a terrible thing. For 18 months, the 550 workers here at Bell Bay Aluminium have faced that uncertainty. They've been putting decisions about their future on hold, whether to buy a house, get another dog, or maybe even to start a family. They then had to go through watching Liberty go through the toughest of times.

data.title: Securing the Future of Bell Bay Aluminium
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese and Rockliff Governments are securing the future of Bell Bay Aluminium smelter, supporting the facility’s 550 workers, their families and the 1,000 workers indirectly employed across Northern Tasmania. We want to see Australia make more things here.This investment will boost jobs in the region while strengthening our national sovereignty.The Bell Bay smelter is a major contributor to Tasmania's industrial and manufacturing sectors and is vital to the Northern Tasmanian regional economy.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47669.label: Securing the Future of Bell Bay Aluminium

data.title: Launch of Three Shocks
data.author: PMC
data.summary: I begin by acknowledging the traditional owners of the land on which we meet, and I pay my respects to elders past, present and emerging.It is such a pleasure to be here tonight for the launch of Three Shocks – Who We Are Becoming in the 21st Century.In this age of shrinking attention spans, George Megalogenis stands out as a rarity.With his eye for detail and his capacity for joining the dots, George makes a valuable contribution to the national discourse every time he hits the keyboard.

data.title: Press conference - Footscray
data.author: PMC
data.summary: DANIEL MULINO, ASSISTANT TREASURER: Hi, I'm Daniel Mulino. It's great to be here in Melbourne's west in my electorate for an announcement in relation to a very significant transport and infrastructure project. The Melbourne Airport Rail Link is going to transform transport in the West and also be a major economic contributor to Victoria. This is a project that is long overdue, so it's wonderful to be here today for this announcement.

data.title: Melbourne Airport Rail Stage 2 set for take-off
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese and Carroll Labor Governments are getting on with building Melbourne Airport Rail Stage 2, with work set to begin in the coming weeks.It will include a new 7.4-kilometre rail line from Albion toward the Airport precinct via a brand-new Keilor East station, as part of the $12 billion joint commitment from the Albanese and Carroll Labor Governments.The line will connect directly to the Metro Tunnel and feature the same high-capacity signalling to enable frequent services.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47666.label: Melbourne Airport Rail Stage 2 set for take-off

data.title: Press conference - Adelaide
data.author: PMC
data.summary: CLAIRE CLUTTERHAM, MEMBER FOR STURT: Good morning everyone, my name is Claire Clutterham and I’m the federal Member for Sturt in the Australian Parliament and it is a pleasure to be here this morning at Hampstead Barracks. I’m joined by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Assistant Minister for Defence Peter Khalil, and our South Australian Premier, Peter Malinauskas. And this morning we are talking about an issue that is at the heart of the Federal Government’s agenda and at the heart of the State Government’s agenda, and that is housing supply. PM, welcome to Adelaide.

data.title: Accelerating the delivery of more homes for South Australians
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese and Malinauskas Governments are working together to fast-track more housing for South Australians, through the redevelopment of two key Defence sites near the Adelaide CBD.Hampstead Barracks was recently identified as a property for divestment, as part of the Australian Government’s response to the independent Defence Estate Audit. The Audit identified sites surplus to Defence’s need, with no clear or ongoing link to capabilities or keeping Australians safe.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47664.label: Accelerating the delivery of more homes for South Australians

data.title: Press conference - Launceston, Tas

data.title: More fans, closer to the action as new stand opens at Launceston's UTAS stadium
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Work on the new Western Stand at Launceston’s UTAS stadium is now complete. It’s another major milestone on the $130 million development of the facility, funded by the Albanese and Rockliff Governments.The new Western Stand repurposes previously unused space between the stand and the pitch, with the new infill seating giving an extra 1,500 fans a front row seat to the action.Spectators will now enjoy modern facilities with wider concourse areas, improving patron circulation and better match-day experiences.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47661.label: More fans, closer to the action as new stand opens at Launceston's UTAS stadium

data.title: Doorstop - Sydney
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Australia is leading on digital safety because we want to keep Australians safe. We're living in an age of artificial intelligence. We want to shape this technology in Australia’s national interest, rather than have it shape us. We now know that it wasn't just the issue of the Australian sites that have been subject to AI agents accessing information without authorisation. There are dozens of cases, including US government sites.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47658.label: Australia's National Statement - United States, New York

data.title: Press conference - New York
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Thanks for joining me. I want to update Australians on an incident in which an artificial intelligence agent has infiltrated an Australian Government website. This incident occurred in June of this year and involved an OpenAI agent gaining unauthorised access into the public-facing Medicare statistics reporting service portal, which is administered by Services Australia. The AI agent accessed both public and non-public files.

data.title: Remarks, Australia-Ukraine meeting
data.author: PMC

Thank you very much for real support, specific one, military support, energy support, which was absolutely crucial, humanitarian. Thank you very much for the benefit and for your support, and that you [are] politically and geopolitically, always with us.

data.title: Agreement on long-term support and cooperation between Australia and Ukraine

data.summary: Today Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed the Australia–Ukraine Bilateral Security Agreement. The Agreement provides a framework for defence and security cooperation and affirms Australia’s enduring commitment to Ukraine.After more than four years of defending itself against Russia’s unprovoked and unjustified invasion, Ukraine has developed one of the world’s most innovative and agile fighting forces.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47648.label: Agreement on long-term support and cooperation between Australia and Ukraine

data.author: PMC

Our position on its future and the future of global relations is clear – global challenges cannot be solved by countries acting alone. Especially right now, when we are facing one of the toughest periods in modern history. The war in the Middle East, an ongoing land war in Europe, the global inflation crisis, the fuel crisis and the rise of AI are incredibly serious challenges.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47649.label: P4M Summit: Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity

But humans need to be in control of it. If it’s going to be successful, then we need to make sure that humans are at the centre of everything that occurs.

data.title: Australia-EU meeting 2026
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The President of the European Council, Antonio Costa, the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen and the Prime Minister of Australia, Anthony Albanese met on 21 September in the margins of the United Nations General Assembly.Presidents Costa and von der Leyen and Prime Minister Albanese reviewed the progress made in deepening cooperation across many fields since President von der Leyen’s visit to Australia in March 2026:

data.title: Climate Week Keynote Address
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Thank you for the invitation to officially open Climate Group’s Climate Week NYC 2026.It’s great to be here with so many champions of climate action.Your CEO – Helen Clarkson.Your Chair – my friend Mike Rann.And of course, Ed Milliband.Last year my Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Chris Bowen, addressed this gathering with a message of hope about the vast global move towards renewables now underway.Climate Group and Australia have a long and strong relationship, going back to the organisation’s early days.

data.title: Australia launches bid for United Nations Security Council seat
data.author: PMC
data.summary: At a time of global uncertainty and major challenges, Australia is an untiring advocate for peace and security. We understand that this is best achieved through international cooperation, which is why we are launching our campaign for a seat on the United Nations Security Council, to serve a two-year term from 2029 to 2030.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47644.label: Australia launches bid for United Nations Security Council seat

data.title: Press conference - United Nations, New York
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: I'm very proud today to be launching Australia’s campaign for a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council for 2029 and 2030. Australia is the best country on earth, and I firmly believe that our best days are ahead of us. And we have an opportunity through this potential seat on the UN Security Council to play a key role in shaping the global issues that really matter to Australians. We’ve been reminded in recent times of how important the interconnectedness in today’s globalised world is.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47643.label: Press conference - United Nations, New York

Australia is, of course, a world leader when it comes to dealing with the issues of safety, when it comes to new technology and the digital economy.

data.title: Visit to California and New York

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47638.label: Visit to California and New York

data.title: Australia ranked 8th in global gender equality rankings
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Australia has ranked 8th in the World Economic Forum’s 2026 Global Gender Gap Report, breaking into to the top ten and achieving its highest ever ranking for gender equality, out of 148 countries.This result reflects the Albanese Government’s sustained action to improve the lives of women and girls, including lifting wages in female-dominated industries, expanding Paid Parental Leave to six months with superannuation, and making significant investments in women’s health.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47637.label: Australia ranked 8th in global gender equality rankings

data.title: Little wings flying high
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese Government is providing another $1 million for Little Wings to help seriously ill children in regional communities access the health care they need.The funding will extend the Government’s support for Little Wings for a further two years, helping families across regional NSW, Queensland and the ACT access the specialist health care their children need.The Government will also match every dollar raised by 12-year-old Dusty Langby, who has walked an incredible 540 kilometres from Warren, NSW to Parliament House in Canberra in support of Little Wings.

data.title: Press conference - Admiralty House

data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning. Today is an exciting day for an extraordinary Australian. A familiar face to just about every Australian I think, no matter where they live. For several decades, Melissa Doyle AM has beamed in the living rooms right around the country through a distinguished career as a television presenter, an author, and a journalist. But her footprint through our great community spans well beyond that. She is a champion for Australian children, for Australian sport, and importantly for Australian charities as well.

data.title: Appointment of new Chair for National Australia Day Council Board
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese Government is pleased to announce Ms Melissa Doyle AM as the new Chair of the National Australia Day Council Board.Ms Doyle has had a distinguished career as a television presenter, author and journalist, with more than 30 years of experience.In the 2016 Australia Day Honours List, Ms Doyle was appointed a Member of the Order of Australia, recognising her significant service to the community through roles with a range of charities and in broadcast media.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47634.label: Appointment of new Chair for National Australia Day Council Board

data.title: 25th commemoration of September 11
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Today marks 25 years since the terrorist attacks of 11 September 2001, which claimed the lives of thousands of innocent people in the United States and from countries around the world.On this solemn day, we remember the 2,977 people killed in New York, Washington DC and in Pennsylvania, including 10 Australians whose lives were tragically cut short far from home.We acknowledge the grief carried by their loved ones. We also honour the courage and selflessness shown in the face of unimaginable horror.

data.title: Lasting Legacy: A new era for the Hunter as M1 extension opens

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47629.label: Lasting Legacy: A new era for the Hunter as M1 extension opens

data.title: My Feed, My Way
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese Government is taking the next step following its world leading social media age ban to ensure Australians have more choice online, with draft legislation for the Digital Duty of Care released today for targeted consultation.These new laws will put the onus on digital service providers to provide a safe online environment, setting minimum standards for the features and tools they use.This will include an Australian first, “My Feed, My Way,” initiative which will give Australians control over their social media algorithms.

data.title: Doubling down on a brave deal to save our children
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Last year, Australia took world-leading action by banning children under the age of 16 from having social media accounts.It was one of the biggest social and cultural changes our country has ever faced, and itwas led by Australian parents protecting children.When we proposed and introduced the ban, there were sceptics, there still are.We didn’t lead the world for the sake of it.We took action because the community said enough was enough and we would no longer let Australian kids be treated as commodities instead of children.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47625.label: Doubling down on a brave deal to save our children

data.title: Pacific collaboration on climate and renewable energy powers ahead

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47623.label: Pacific collaboration on climate and renewable energy powers ahead

data.title: Vale Bruce Baird
data.author: PMC
data.summary: With the passing of Bruce Baird, Australia has lost a real gentleman and a true parliamentarian. Bruce had the uncommon distinction of serving his nation as a Liberal member at both the state and federal level, including as Transport Minister in the Greiner NSW Government. It was a portfolio he handled with such aplomb that I was pleased to appoint him years later as the inaugural chair of the National Heavy Vehicle Regulator Board.Then of course there was his glittering success as the minister in charge of Sydney’s bid for the 2000 Olympic Games.

data.title: Pre-COP Leaders’ Event in Fiji and Tuvalu
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Fiji and Tuvalu from 5 to 7 October 2026 for the Pre-COP Leaders’ event. At COP30, Australia secured the role of COP31 President of Negotiations and agreement to deliver a Pacific-hosted Pre-COP, including a special Leaders’ event. Australia will co-host the event with Fiji and Tuvalu.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47672.label: Pre-COP Leaders’ Event in Fiji and Tuvalu

data.title: Doorstop - Nadi, Fiji
data.author: PMC
data.summary: It's wonderful to be here in Fiji and to also be visiting Tuvalu in what is the important meeting leading up to the Climate Change Conference next month. It is important that Pacific voices are heard, because the Pacific is the front line of action on climate change. For many of the nations represented by leaders here, it is literally a threat to their very existence, which is why the world must act. We know that we're seeing more intense and more extreme weather events, more frequent on occasion, because of the science on climate change has told us that that would occur.
